title: Every example given, and still we argue most.
subtitle: The human habit of debating the truth

row.title: a clever excuse
sub: If Allah wills, He'll wake us

then: Allah has explained matters clearly, yet {trap}man is very quarrelsome and opposes truth with falsehood{/trap}. Ali reported the Prophet ﷺ visited him and Fatimah at night and asked if they would pray. Ali replied that their souls were in Allah's Hand. The Prophet ﷺ walked away {idea}slapping his thigh and reciting this verse{/idea}.
now: The alarm for Fajr goes off and your mind instantly builds a case: I am tired, Allah is merciful, I will make it up. {idea}You are arguing with the reminder instead of answering it.{/idea}
old: I have good reasons for not doing it right now.
new: Sometimes my reasons are just me arguing with a clear reminder.
try: The next time you catch yourself arguing against a good deed today, stop debating and do it.

title: What are they waiting for, the punishment itself?
subtitle: Guidance came, and they still held out
then: Ibn Kathir says nothing stopped them except {trap}their demand to witness with their own eyes the punishment{/trap} they were warned about. Past peoples said, bring it down on us. The Quraysh said, if this is true, rain stones on us. Yet {idea}guidance had already come to them{/idea}.
now: You keep saying you will get serious about prayer after a sign. After the health scare. After the funeral. {idea}The sign is already in your hands.{/idea} Asking forgiveness does not need a disaster first.
old: I will change when something big makes me.
new: Guidance is already here. I do not need to wait for a shock.
try: Ask Allah's forgiveness today for one thing, without waiting for a reason.

title: Messengers bring good news and warning. Some answer with mockery.
subtitle: Arguing to knock the truth down
then: Messengers come {reward}giving good news to those who believe{/reward} and warning those who reject. Some argue with falsehood {trap}to weaken the truth{/trap}, but cannot. Ibn Kathir calls making fun of Allah's signs {trap}the worst type of disbelief{/trap}.
now: Someone in the group chat posts a meme mocking prayer or hijab. Everyone sends laughing faces, and your thumb hovers over one too. {idea}Laughing along is a small step in the same direction.{/idea}
old: A joke about religion is just a joke.
new: Turning Allah's signs into a joke is never small.
try: Next time religion is mocked around you, simply do not join in. Silence is enough.

title: Reminded, he turned away and forgot his own deeds.
subtitle: The heart that closes after ignoring
then: Ibn Kathir explains the worst wrong is to be {trap}reminded of the signs of Allah and then turn away{/trap}, not listening or paying attention, while forgetting one's own bad deeds. Their hearts come to have coverings so {trap}they will not understand this Qur'an{/trap}.
now: The khutbah lands on you exactly, and you are checking your phone before the prayer ends. A friend gently names a habit and you change the subject. {idea}Every ignored reminder makes the next one harder to hear.{/idea}
old: I can ignore this reminder and catch the next one.
new: Each reminder I turn from makes my heart a little harder to reach.
try: Act on one reminder you received this week, however small, before tonight.

title: Your Lord is Forgiving, full of mercy, and patient.
subtitle: Why the punishment is not rushed
then: Right after the warning, Allah reminds His Messenger ﷺ that {reward}your Lord is forgiving and has great mercy{/reward}. Ibn Kathir says He is patient, conceals faults, forgives sins, and {idea}may guide some of them from wrongdoing to true guidance{/idea}. But the time is fixed.
now: You did something wrong years ago and nothing bad followed. You assumed it did not matter. {idea}Allah is not ignoring you. He is giving you room to come back.{/idea}
old: Nothing happened to me, so it must not matter.
new: The delay is mercy, giving me time to turn back.
try: Think of one past wrong you never repented for, and repent for it today.

title: Those towns had an appointed time too.
subtitle: Ruins as reminders
then: This refers to earlier nations destroyed {trap}because of their stubborn disbelief{/trap}, each with a set time limit. Ibn Kathir explains the address to the idolators of Makkah: {idea}you are not dearer to Us than them{/idea}, so beware.
now: It is easy to read about past nations and feel safe. {idea}The point is not them. It is you{/idea}, and the quiet belief that you are the exception to the rule.
old: Warnings in the Quran are about other people.
new: No one is dearer to Allah than His rules. I read these warnings for myself.
try: Read one warning verse today as if it was written to you personally.

title: A prophet sets out to learn, however long it takes.
subtitle: Musa's journey to someone who knew more
then: The Prophet ﷺ said Musa was asked who was the most learned, and said {trap}I am{/trap}. Allah rebuked him because {idea}he did not refer the knowledge to Allah{/idea}, and told him of a servant at the junction of the two seas who knew more. Musa set out with Yusha bin Nun, ready to travel even a lifetime.
now: You are the one at work everyone asks. You have answers for every family debate. {idea}The moment you feel you know the most is the moment to go and learn.{/idea}
old: I already know enough about this.
new: There is always someone who knows more. Knowledge belongs to Allah.
try: Ask someone today to teach you one thing you do not know, and listen fully.

title: At the meeting point, the fish slipped into the sea.
subtitle: The sign they were looking for, missed
then: Musa had been told that {idea}where you lose the fish, you will find him{/idea}. They slept at a rock. The fish moved, fell into the sea, and Allah held back the water so its path was {reward}like a tunnel{/reward}. They forgot it and walked on.
now: You were praying for direction and the answer came as an odd thing that went wrong. A cancelled flight, a missed bus, a closed door. {idea}Sometimes the sign is the thing you lost.{/idea}
old: Things going wrong are just bad luck.
new: A small loss can be the very sign I asked Allah for.
try: Think of one recent small loss and ask what it might be pointing you toward.

title: Past the right place, the tiredness hit.
subtitle: Fatigue as a signal
then: They walked the rest of the day and the whole night. The hadith says {idea}Musa did not feel tired until he passed the place Allah had ordered him to go to{/idea}. Then he said: bring our meal, {trap}we have suffered fatigue in this journey{/trap}.
now: You push through months at a job or a path that felt right, then suddenly everything drains you. {idea}Sometimes the exhaustion is a sign you have walked past where you were meant to stop.{/idea}
old: Feeling drained just means I need to push harder.
new: Sometimes tiredness is telling me to look back at where I missed the turn.
try: If something is draining you lately, sit quietly for five minutes and ask Allah where you should stop.

title: I forgot the fish, and owned up to it.
subtitle: Yusha admits his mistake
then: When Musa asked for the meal, Yusha told him plainly: {trap}I indeed forgot the fish{/trap}, and none but Shaytan made me forget to mention it. The hadith adds that the path was a tunnel for the fish and {idea}a wonder for Musa and his servant{/idea}.
now: You forgot to send the file, missed the deadline, left the stove on. Your boss asks. {idea}The honest I forgot is what lets the whole team turn back in time.{/idea}
old: Admitting my mistake will make things worse.
new: Owning a mistake quickly lets everyone get back on the right road.
try: Own up today to one small thing you forgot or got wrong, plainly and without excuses.

title: That is what we were seeking. So they went back.
subtitle: Turning around without blame
then: Musa did not scold Yusha. He heard the news and said, {idea}this is what we have been looking for{/idea}. Then {reward}they went back, following their own footprints{/reward}, to the rock.
now: Your child forgets something important and you feel the anger rise. Or you realize you took the wrong turn and the whole car is tense. {idea}Name it, turn around, and keep going together.{/idea}
old: When someone's mistake costs me, I need to make it clear.
new: The mistake showed the way. Turning back calmly is part of the journey.
try: When someone slips today, skip the blame and say: okay, let us go back and fix it.

title: They found a servant given mercy and knowledge from Allah.
subtitle: Meeting Al-Khidr
then: They found a man covered with a cloth at the rock. Ibn Kathir says this was {idea}Al-Khidr, as the authentic hadiths indicate{/idea}. Allah describes him first as one {reward}on whom We bestowed mercy{/reward}, then as one taught knowledge from Him.
now: You meet someone with a modest job who seems to see things you miss. No degree on the wall, but deep wisdom. {idea}Knowledge from Allah does not always come with a title.{/idea}
old: The wisest person is the one with the most qualifications.
new: Allah gives mercy and knowledge to whom He wills, often quietly.
try: Ask an older, quiet person in your life for one piece of advice this week.
